title: Lesson 12
subtitle: Japanese Verbs — Polite verb conjugation and the particle ni
objectives: Learn how to conjugate verbs into the polite forms: ~masu, ~masen, ~mashita, ~masen deshita
Conjugate the four lesson verbs: iku, kuru, kaeru, wakaru
Use the location particle ni (and e) to say where you are going
Use the time particle ni for 'in', 'on', 'at' — and know when NOT to use it
Build languages and nationalities with ~go and ~jin
Ask and answer: Doko ni ikimasu ka / Itsu kimasu ka / Nani go ga hanasemasu ka

vocab.english: to return, go back, go home, come back, come home (regular verb)
It has been a long time.

vocab.japanese: きょうは あついですね

grammar.title: Polite versus informal speaking
grammar.pattern: use polite verb forms with strangers and people of higher status
grammar.explanation: It is common to use polite language with people you don't know or who have higher social status than yourself (a stranger on the street, your boss). With family, friends, or people of lower or equal status, informal speech is more natural. Until your Japanese is more advanced, stick to polite Japanese to form good speaking habits.

examples.japanese: とうきょう に いきます。
examples.english: I am going to Tokyo. (polite form)

mistakes: Using informal forms with strangers or your boss before your Japanese is advanced

grammar.title: The dictionary form and verb types
grammar.pattern: all verbs in the dictionary form end with a う form hiragana
grammar.explanation: The dictionary form is the most basic form of the verb with no conjugation — it is the only version in the dictionary, and the most important form to memorize. Every Japanese verb in the dictionary form ends with a う form hiragana: いく ends with く, and くる, わかる and かえる all end in る. Verbs are labeled regular (they all follow the exact same conjugation pattern) or irregular (no logical rule — patterns must be memorized; luckily there are only a small number).

examples.japanese: いく
くる
かえる
examples.english: to return, go back, go home — regular

examples.japanese: わかる

mistakes: Assuming くる follows the regular conjugation pattern — it is irregular

grammar.title: Making the conversion: change the last hiragana into the い form
grammar.pattern: regular verb dictionary form → final hiragana switched to い form
grammar.explanation: To make the polite versions of regular verbs, first change the final hiragana of the dictionary form into the い form: move straight up the hiragana chart column (る→り, る→り, く→き). This pattern will NOT work for irregular verbs such as くる (to come) — only for regular verbs.

examples.japanese: わかる → わかり
かえる → かえり
いく → いき

mistakes: Applying the い form conversion to the irregular verb くる

grammar.title: Polite verb endings
grammar.explanation: After changing the dictionary form into the い form, add one of four endings: ~ます (will~, do~, am going to~), ~ません (won't~, don't~), ~ました (did~), ~ませんでした (didn't~). Example: わかり + ます = わかります (do understand); いき + ませんでした = いきませんでした (didn't go).

examples.japanese: わかります / わかりません / わかりました / わかりませんでした
examples.english: do understand / do not understand / understood / didn't understand

examples.japanese: いきます / いきません / いきました / いきませんでした
examples.english: will go / won't go / went / didn't go

examples.japanese: かえります / かえりません / かえりました / かえりませんでした
examples.english: will return / will not return / returned / didn't return

mistakes: Using ~ました for the negative past — the past negative is ~ませんでした

grammar.title: Conjugating the irregular verb くる
grammar.pattern: くる → き + ます / ません / ました / ませんでした
grammar.explanation: くる (to come) is the only irregular verb in this lesson. Irregular verbs don't follow the chart — their patterns must be memorized. くる becomes きます (will come, do come), きません (won't come, don't come), きました (came), きませんでした (didn't come).

examples.japanese: あした、きますか。
いいえ、いきません。

mistakes: Saying くります or くりません — くる drops to き, it never becomes きり

grammar.title: Location particles に and へ
grammar.explanation: に and へ (written へ but pronounced え) are location and destination particles placed after locations; both can mean 'to'. に is used when going to an exact location ('I am going to France'); へ is used when going in a general direction ('I am going to the south'). In modern Japan most people freely mix them. From this point on the book uses に as the standard location and destination marker — the key point is that locations require a location marker.

examples.japanese: とうきょう に
がっこう に
ぎんこう に
にほん に

mistakes: Forgetting the location marker after a place: say とうきょう に いきます, not just とうきょう いきます

grammar.title: Time particle に
grammar.explanation: に also marks time in a sentence, meaning 'in', 'on', or 'at': いちがつ に (in January), かようび に (on Tuesday), ろくじ に (at six o'clock).

examples.japanese: いちがつ に い ます。
かようび に い まし た。

mistakes: Adding に to relative time words like きょう or あした

grammar.title: No に with きょう、あした、らいしゅう etc.
grammar.pattern: relative time words take NO particle
grammar.explanation: Words like きょう (today), あした (tomorrow), らいしゅう (next week), きのう (yesterday), きょねん (last year), こんしゅう (this week) are not 'specific times' like Monday or January. Adding に would be as strange as saying 'I am going ON tomorrow'. Easy rule: 'If you don't use IN, ON, or AT in English, then don't use に in Japanese.'

examples.japanese: らいしゅう い ます。
examples.english: I am going next week. (no に)

examples.japanese: きのう い まし た。
きょねん い ませ ん でし た。
こんしゅう い ませ ん。
examples.english: I am not going this week.

mistakes: Saying あした に いきます — drop the に with words like tomorrow, today, next week

grammar.title: Sentence structure using verbs
grammar.explanation: Verbs always come last in Japanese sentences. Just like か is added to です to make a question, you can add か after the conjugated verb to make a question: どこ に い ます か。(Where are you going?) / いえ に かえり まし た か。(Did you return home?)

examples.japanese: どこ に い ます か。
にほん に い ます。
いつ き ます か。
なん にち に い ます か。
examples.english: What day of the month are you going?

mistakes: Putting the verb anywhere other than the end of the sentence

grammar.title: Using the verb わかる with が
grammar.pattern: [thing understood] + が + わかります
grammar.explanation: When using わかる to say you understand something, you must use が to mark the thing that you understand: にほんご が わかり ます (I understand Japanese).

examples.japanese: にほんご が わかり ます。
にほんご が わかり ませ ん。
かれ は えいご が わかり ませ ん。

mistakes: Using は or を instead of が to mark what you understand

grammar.title: Languages and nationalities with ～ご and ～じん
grammar.explanation: By adding ご (language) and じん (people) after a country name you create languages and nationalities: supein (Spain) → supein ご (Spanish language), roshia (Russia) → roshia じん (Russian person). Japan: にほん → にほんじん / にほんご; Korea: かんこく → かんこくじん / かんこくご; China: ちゅうごく → ちゅうごくじん / ちゅうごくご. Note: this works for many countries but not all — America (amerika) speaks えいご, the Philippines (firipin) speaks tagaragu ご, Mexico (mekishiko) speaks supein ご.

examples.japanese: Furansu ご が わかり ます か。
Jon さん は kanada じん です。
examples.romaji: Jon san wa kanada jin desu.

examples.japanese: ようこさん は supein ご が はなせ ます。
examples.romaji: Youko san wa supein go ga hanasemasu.

mistakes: Assuming every country's language name is [country] + ご — America uses えいご, not amerika ご

exercises.prompt: Match the four lesson verbs with their meanings:

pairs.right: to return, go back, go home

exercises.explanation: The four verbs taught in Lesson 12.

exercises.prompt: Which verb in this lesson is irregular?
exercises.explanation: The book: the only verb in this lesson that isn't regular is くる (come).

exercises.prompt: In the dictionary form, every Japanese verb ends with...
exercises.explanation: All verbs in the dictionary form end with う form hiragana — く and る are both う form.

exercises.prompt: What is the dictionary form of a verb?
choices: The most basic form, with no conjugation — the only version in the dictionary
The most formal form used in writing
exercises.explanation: The dictionary form is the most basic form without any conjugation — and the most important form to memorize.

exercises.prompt: Step 1 of the polite conversion: わかる → わか___ (change the last hiragana to the い form).
exercises.explanation: る moves straight up the column to り: wakaru → wakari.

exercises.prompt: The い form conversion pattern works for...
exercises.explanation: The pattern will NOT work for irregular verbs such as くる — only for regular verbs.

exercises.prompt: Match the polite endings with their meanings:
exercises.explanation: The four polite verb endings.

exercises.prompt: I went: いき___ (past positive polite ending).
exercises.explanation: いき + ました = いきました (went).

exercises.prompt: Didn't go: いき___ (past negative polite ending).
exercises.explanation: いき + ませんでした = いきませんでした (didn't go).

exercises.prompt: ぎんこう に いきました
choices: I will go to the bank.
I didn't go to the bank.
exercises.explanation: Ginkou ni ikimashita = I went to the bank.

exercises.prompt: おおさか に いませ ん
choices: I am not going to Osaka.
exercises.explanation: Oosaka ni ikimasen = I am not going to Osaka (example sentence 4, p.239).

exercises.prompt: I didn't go to school: がっこう に いませ___ (polite past negative).
exercises.explanation: がっこう に いませ ん でし た = I didn't go to school.

exercises.prompt: Which particle is used when going to an EXACT location, like France?
exercises.explanation: に is used when going to an exact location; へ is used when going in a general direction.

exercises.prompt: The particle へ is written with 'he' but pronounced...
exercises.explanation: Although written as へ, it is pronounced as え.

exercises.prompt: I am going to school: がっこう ___ いきます (location particle).
exercises.explanation: Locations require a location marker — the book uses に as the standard one.

exercises.prompt: What does いちがつ に mean?
exercises.explanation: いちがつ に = in January — に with time means 'in', 'on', or 'at'.

exercises.prompt: Why is it 'らいしゅう い ます' and NOT 'らいしゅう に い ます'?
choices: らいしゅう is not a specific time like Monday or January — no に needed
らいしゅう already contains に
に can only be used once per sentence
It is a typo in the book
exercises.explanation: Rule: if you don't use IN, ON, or AT in English, don't use に in Japanese.

exercises.prompt: Which is correct for 'I didn't go last year'?
choices: きょねん に い ませ ん でし た。
きょねん い ませ ん でし た。
きょねん い まし た。
きょねん に い まし た。
exercises.explanation: きょねん (last year) takes no に, and the past negative is いませ ん でし た.

exercises.prompt: らいしゅう い ます
choices: I am not going next week.
exercises.explanation: Raishuu ikimasu = I am going next week (no に after raishuu).

exercises.prompt: Order the words: I am going to Tokyo.
exercises.explanation: [location] + に + verb — verbs always come last: とうきょう に い ます。

exercises.prompt: どこ に い ます か
exercises.explanation: Doko ni ikimasu ka = Where are you going (to)?

exercises.prompt: いつ き ます か
exercises.explanation: Itsu kimasu ka = When are you coming?

exercises.prompt: Order the words: Did you return home?
tokens: かえり まし た
exercises.explanation: いえ に かえり まし た か。 — か comes after the conjugated verb to make a question.

exercises.prompt: No, I didn't go. But I will go tomorrow: いいえ、いませ___。でも、あした い ます。
exercises.explanation: From the Q&A: いいえ、い ませ ん でし た。でも、あした い ます。

exercises.prompt: Which particle marks the thing you understand with わかる?
exercises.explanation: When using わかる, you must use が to mark the thing you understand: にほんご が わかり ます。

exercises.prompt: にほんご が わかり ませ ん
exercises.explanation: Nihongo ga wakarimasen = I don't understand Japanese.

exercises.prompt: Spain is 'supein' in Japanese. How do you say 'Spanish language'?
exercises.explanation: Add ご (language) after a country name: supein ご = Spanish language; supein じん would be a Spanish person.

exercises.prompt: Match the country with its language:
exercises.explanation: Note the exception: America's language is えいご, not 'amerika ご'.

exercises.prompt: Jon is Canadian: Jon さん は kanada ___ です。
exercises.explanation: Add じん (people/nationality) after a country: kanada じん です。

exercises.prompt: You meet an old friend you haven't seen for years. What do you say?
choices: どこに いきますか。
exercises.explanation: おひさしぶりです = It has been a long time.

exercises.prompt: なにご が はなせますか
exercises.explanation: New phrase: なにご が はなせますか = What languages can you speak?

exercises.prompt: I will return tomorrow: あした かえり___。
exercises.explanation: From the Q&A: あした かえり ます。(I will return tomorrow — no に after あした.)

exercises.prompt: Order the words: I don't understand Japanese.
exercises.explanation: にほんご が わかり ませ ん。 — が marks the thing understood; the verb comes last.

exercises.prompt: In the short dialogue, Mr. Tanaka says 'きょうは あついですね'. What does he mean?
choices: It has been a long time.
From now on I will study.
exercises.explanation: New expression from the dialogue: きょうは あついですね = Today sure is hot.

quiz.prompt: In a Japanese sentence, the verb always comes...
quiz.explanation: Verbs always come last in Japanese sentences.

quiz.prompt: What does きました mean?
quiz.explanation: The irregular verb くる: き + ました = きました (came).

quiz.prompt: Won't come, don't come: き___ (polite present negative of くる).
quiz.explanation: くる conjugates irregularly: き ませ ん = won't come, don't come.

quiz.prompt: がっこう に いませ ん でし た
choices: I am not going to school.
quiz.explanation: Example sentence 3: がっこう に い ませ ん でし た = I didn't go to school.
なに じん です か = What nationality are you? (I am Mexican: Mekishiko じん です。)

quiz.prompt: すいようびに かえりました
quiz.explanation: From the Q&A: すいようび に かえり まし た = I came back on Wednesday.

summary: Four verbs (いく, くる, かえる, わかる) meet four polite endings: change the last hiragana of the dictionary form to the い form (regular verbs only — くる is irregular and must be memorized), then add ~masu (will/do), ~masen (won't/don't), ~mashita (did) or ~masen deshita (didn't). Locations and destinations take に (へ is also possible, pronounced え); specific times take に for 'in/on/at', but relative words like きょう、あした、らいしゅう take no に — if you don't use IN, ON or AT in English, don't use に in Japanese. Verbs always end the sentence, and か after the verb makes a question. Mark what you understand with が (にほんご が わかります), and build languages with ～ご and nationalities with ～じん.
